task: Fix the timeout failure in the batch processor after the external API rate limit was not respected.

candidate_memories.content: Batch processor fails with 429 errors because it sends requests at 200 rps exceeding the partner API's 100 rps limit.
The batch processor must throttle requests to 80 rps to stay under the partner API's 100 rps limit with headroom.
The rate limit was increased from 50 rps to 200 rps without checking the partner API's published limit.
The 429 errors cause the batch to fail after 3 retries; no data is processed once the rate limit is hit.
Session 8 note: the operations team observed 429 errors peaking during the morning batch window at 9:00 AM.
The partner API has a documented 100 requests per second rate limit per API key.
Session 6 note: the integration team registered a second API key to double the effective rate limit.
Old practice: the batch processor had a 50 rps limit based on the initial API contract.
The partner API rate limit response includes a Retry-After header with the next available window.
Session 11 note: a batch performance test showed the processor reaches 200 rps peak on large batches.
Old rate limit guide: the 50 rps limit was set before the partner increased their capacity.
Batch processors must throttle to 80% of the partner API rate limit to maintain a safety margin.
Session 4 note: the monitoring team added a 429 rate limit response counter to the dashboard.
The batch processor distributes requests using a token bucket with configurable refill rate.
A throughput test in session 9 confirmed the processor handles 50 rps without any 429 errors.
The partner API also enforces a concurrent connection limit of 10 simultaneous connections.
Before increasing batch processor throughput, validate the new rate against the partner API contract.
Session 7 note: the integration team added exponential backoff for 429 errors.
Old batch config: the processor was configured for 50 rps matching the early API contract limit.
Batch processing jobs are scheduled during off-peak hours to reduce impact on the partner API.
